scientific_question: Does the short-horizon gain from composing the accepted QK read map with dense complete experts persist through the matched 5TPP horizon without any residual-write or expert-matrix compression?

forbidden_changes: generated V or any residual-write projection
generated, shared, or factorized expert matrices
router, optimizer, learning rate, data, seeds, or horizon changes
automatic rerun, parallel arm, or post-result threshold change

decision_rule.pass: Confirm 5TPP horizon compatibility of generated QK with dense complete experts. Return to theory-gated expert representability work; do not infer generated-expert viability or automatically extend to 20TPP or a larger rung.
decision_rule.fail: Reject horizon-stable composition despite the 0.5TPP gain. Retain the standalone QK-only and dense-complete-expert controls; do not sweep capacity or modify expert matrices.

monitoring.performance_preflight: foreground-polled because it must finish within five minutes
monitoring.scientific_run: one terminal-or-error invocation callback with explicit @Codex action prompt

theory.positive_claim: The experiment tests composition and horizon stability of one accepted read-map compression with dense conditional experts.
theory.claim_boundary: It does not compress attention V/O, expert c_fc/c_proj, inference parameters, or expert FLOPs, and it does not test full replacement.
theory.causal_reason: The 0.5TPP composition passed every checkpoint by at least 0.0068 CE and finished 0.2713 CE below dense MoE. A matched 5TPP confirmation is the sole follow-up authorized by that preregistered result.
